properties.statement: [BL-143] No vocabulary for "it runs but the answers are wrong" — so an opinion gets recorded as a measurement, which is the evidence-quality family's FOURTH axis
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by an /adopt pass over music_graph, a ~11k-LOC Python research repo taken from an empty graph to 134 nodes / 379 edges. Reported in that project's own reflow2_feedback.txt.* This repo's central fact is that everything executes and almost nothing is correct, and Verification.status offers only planned/passing/failing/skipped/blocked. The reporter recorded a smoke run as passing (it truly does run) and an accuracy measurement as failing \u2014 but nothing in the repo states an acceptance threshold, so failing is a judgement smuggled in as data. Their words. The caveat went into the description, *\"where no detector reads it\"*. THIS COMPLETES THE [BL-106]/[BL-126]/[BL-136] FAMILY WITH A FOURTH FACE. Those three say a check can be stale in TIME, narrow in INPUT SPACE, or not INDEPENDENT of what it validates \u2014 all answering *how good is the evidence*. This one is one step earlier: there is no criterion, so there is nothing for the evidence to be evidence OF. A failing with no threshold and a failing against a stated one are indistinguishable, which is the same flattering-collapse the family exists to break. Corroborated from the other side by [W7] in the same document: having to write *\"marked failing because the owner says so, NOT because a threshold exists\"* into a description felt wrong enough that it became the question put to the owner \u2014 which produced that project's first acceptance criterion in seven months. The pressure worked; it just came from an agent feeling awkward rather than from the schema. Fix shapes: a status: inconclusive; or a criterion field required alongside failing; or the same fact as a relation, matching how the family recorded the other three axes rather than adding a property. Do not let this be answered by prose in a description \u2014 that is where this instance already went to die. Size M SHAPE DECIDED 2026-08-01, on Anthony's call from three options (dec:a-failing-check-says-against-what, accepted). Verification gains an OPTIONAL criterion \u2014 what the check was measured against. A failing carrying one is reported as a MEASUREMENT; a failing without one is reported as a bar never stated, and is never presented as though a threshold existed. Requiring it was REJECTED on two counts: it breaks every existing failing check until someone supplies a bar retroactively, and it blocks the honest case where something is plainly broken and no threshold was ever written down \u2014 but mainly because it is OUT OF STEP WITH THE FAMILY. [BL-106], [BL-126] and [BL-136] all REPORT the gap rather than refusing the work: an unscoped check is counted unscoped, an undated one unknown, a consumed one consumed, and none is forbidden. This is the fourth axis and it behaves like the other three. A new inconclusive status was also REJECTED \u2014 cheapest, and it gives *it runs but correctness is unknown* a home, but someone can still write failing as a pure opinion and nothing notices, which is the exact defect. Not foreclosed; it simply answers a different question. THE FAMILY IS NOW FOUR FACES OF ONE HOLE: stale in TIME, narrow in INPUT SPACE, not INDEPENDENT of what it validates, and \u2014 this one \u2014 no CRITERION, so there is nothing for the evidence to be evidence OF. The first three ask how good the evidence is; this asks what it was evidence FOR. NOT YET BUILT: the shape is settled, the build is this row.", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-143 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M."}
